newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end slightly higher after late rally.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end slightly higher after late rally.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from a slump in late trading Tuesday to finish slightly higher.

Traders and analysts said the bolsa crossed into positive territory while the Dow Jones industrial average was extending its gains late in the session, though the Mexican rally was a pale shadow of the surge on Wall Street.
"The market did not respond to the Dow Jones. No one believed in yesterday's late gains, and several key blue chips could not stand the pace," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 6.45 points, or 0.17 percent, at 3,805.10.
"Yesterday's rally was make-believe, and so the market returned to its lateral channel today," said an equity analyst who asked no to be named.
"The market is still on a long-term upward trend, which is important but looked fragile today because of forecast sharp hikes in primary rates," he added.
"Most foreign capital has gone to the money market, where they expect primary rates to gain this evening," the trader said.
A Reuters survey showed money market traders were expecting Banco de Mexico to place bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average rate of 23.16 percent, or 83 basis points higher than last week.
Traders said the expected rise in Cetes rates tempered the reaction in the Mexican stock market to strong gains by the Dow industrials, which closed up 135.26 points at 6,587.16.
Dealers said Telmex L shares, which accounted for 17 percent of the 77.95 million shares traded during the session, weighed most on the bourse's last-minute recovery.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.2 centavos firmer at 7.8960/7.8980 per dollar.
Traders said a stronger peso also prompted arbitrage trading in Televisa, whose CPO shares declined 90 centavos to 102.10 pesos, while the media company's ADRs gained 1/2 to 25-3/4.
Financial group GFB's B shares ended up seven centavos at 2.54 pesos after falling sharply on Monday.
"GFB always tends to fall at thin volume," a trader said.
Traders said several blue chips also declined on market expectations of poor first-quarter earnings reports.
Ahmsa declined just four centavos to 16.22 pesos.
On the broad market, 120 stocks changed hands, of which 47 gained while the same number declined.
